claims.text: An emptyDir volume is created when the Pod is assigned to a node and starts empty; when the Pod is removed from the node, its data is deleted permanently; a container crash/restart does not remove the Pod, so the emptyDir data survives it.

A PersistentVolume is a piece of storage in the cluster, a cluster-scoped API object with a lifecycle independent of any Pod; a PersistentVolumeClaim is a namespaced request for storage that asks for a size and access modes.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Storage > Persistent Volumes > Introduction; PersistentVolumeClaims

claims.text: The control plane binds a claim to a PersistentVolume that matches it; the PV may be larger than requested; PVC-to-PV binding is one-to-one and, once bound, exclusive; the claim's status phase becomes Bound.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Persistent Volumes > Lifecycle of a volume and claim > Binding; outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/pvc.txt lines 5-7

claims.text: ReadWriteOnce: the volume can be mounted read-write by a single node; it still allows multiple Pods running on that node to access the volume.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Persistent Volumes > Access Modes (ReadWriteOnce); outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/pvc.txt lines 21-30

claims.text: A Pod uses a claim as a volume with volumes[].persistentVolumeClaim.claimName; the claim must be in the same namespace as the Pod; the Pod never names the PersistentVolume.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Persistent Volumes > Claims As Volumes ('Claims must exist in the same namespace as the Pod using the claim'); data-writer-pod.yaml lines 18-21

claims.text: A claim's volume is mounted on the Pod's node and into the container at the volumeMounts path (data-writer-pod.yaml: /data).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Persistent Volumes > Claims As Volumes ('The volume is then mounted to the host and into the Pod')
